content.title: Karol G’s ICE warning ahead of Coachella 2026: How to watch
content.text: Superstar singer Karol G is making history Sunday night as the first Latina to headline the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in the festival's decades-long run — but comments she made about U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in a new Playboy interview have sparked a controversy her team is now pushing back on.Born and raised in Medellín, Colombia — a city she has credited as a defining influence on her career — Karol G is not a U.S. citizen, making the threat of visa revocation she describes more than hypothetical.Making History on the Main StageKarol G takes the Coachella Stage tonight as the first Latina headliner in the festival's 27-year history, closing out her Tropicoqueta era before an audience that stretches far beyond the Indio, California desert. She follows Justin Bieber, who delivered a successful headlining performance on Saturday night. The milestone hasn't been lost on her. "Being the first Latina headliner sets a really high bar for the show I need to reach," she said. "I want to deliver something from my heart that represents my love for my community and my fans."She's been candid about the pressure she's placed on herself. "I'm putting the pressure on myself to deliver something at such a high level so people can leave the show and say, 'Karol was ready. She was more than ready for this,'" she told Rolling Stone this week.A Warning She Can't IgnoreIn a new Playboy interview for the magazine's Spring 2026 cover, Karol G revealed she has repeatedly been urged not to speak out against ICE — warnings she says come with a clear implied threat. "People will say, 'It's better you don't,'" she told journalist Paola Ramos. "Why? Because if you say the thing, maybe the next day you'll get a call: 'Hey, we are taking your visa away.'"'You Become Bait'The Grammy winner described the dynamic bluntly. "You become bait, because some people want to show their power," she said. The risk is not abstract — even within her own inner circle, speaking out carries consequences. "My team would kill me," she acknowledged, for saying something as simple as "ICE Out." Still, she hasn't ruled it out. "But I'm willing to say it," she insisted.Waiting for the Right MomentRather than acting on impulse, Karol G says she's been deliberate — holding back not out of fear, but out of strategy. "I have a huge stage, and that's why I want to wait, and if someone was ever to do something to me, I want to stand firmly on my stage for my community," she said. "So that's why I may have to be more careful, and wait for my turn, and ensure that, through that opportunity, I can talk and represent something more."Her comments come as immigration enforcement under ICE has become a cultural flashpoint. Puerto Rican star Bad Bunny drew widespread attention earlier this year when he called for "ICE out" while accepting the Best Música Urbana Album award at the 2026 Grammys — a moment Karol G was present for, having appeared at "La Casita" during his 2026 Super Bowl halftime performance.What She's Planning to SayKarol G says she wants her words to land with weight. "What impact does it really have to say 'ICE Out' versus something else that can have a real impact on my community?" she asked during the Playboy interview. The question she keeps returning to is one of purpose and responsibility. "If I'm being honest with you, it's something that crosses the line of what I have to do to protect myself. But at the end of the day, what is my role if I'm in this position?"That nuance is now at the center of a dispute. Sources close to Karol told TMZ this week that her team would never instruct her not to mention ICE or warn her against advocacy in any way — pointing to her foundation's ongoing work supporting immigrant communities in the U.S., including helping immigrant mothers, in some cases assisting those who choose to return to their home countries with dignity. Those sources told the outlet the controversy may stem from a translation issue, as the Playboy interview was originally conducted in Spanish.Per TMZ's sources, Karol's position going into Coachella is not about staying silent — it's about making her words matter. She has said she would speak out with her "whole soul," but wants to fully understand the consequences and what tangible change can come from it. Her team, sources said, would never hold her back from her advocacy.NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 15: Karol G performs during the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show at Steiner Studios on October 15, 2025 in New York City. (...How to Watch TonightKarol G takes the Coachella Stage Sunday, April 12 at 9:55 p.m. PDT, with her set expected to run until approximately 11:55 p.m. Fans can watch free via the Coachella YouTube page and the Coachella app, with select performances available in 4K. She will headline again during the festival's second weekend, April 17-19.
